reconcile.connective: Commentators explain that 'in the day' (Gen 2:4) is idiomatic Hebrew for the whole creative period, not a reference to a single 24-hour day — making the two accounts complementary rather than contradictory.

discrepancy.connective: Robert G. Ingersoll, pressing the plain sense of 'in the day that the LORD God made the earth and heavens' against the six-day sequence of Genesis 1, argued that Genesis presents two incompatible creation timelines that cannot be reconciled by grammatical appeal.

skeptic.name: Robert G. Ingersoll
skeptic.attribution: Robert G. Ingersoll (d. 1899), Some Mistakes of Moses (1879)

excerpts.author: John Gill
excerpts.attribution: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63)
excerpts.excerpt_text: in the day that the Lord God made the earth, and the heavens; meaning not any particular day, not the first day, in which the heavens and the earth were created; but referring to the whole time of the six days, in which everything in them, and relating to them, were made.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Gill directly addresses the tension: 'in the day' (Gen 2:4) is not a competing timeline but a Hebrew idiom encompassing the entire six-day creation week, so the two accounts use 'day' in different senses.

excerpts.author: Tyndale
excerpts.excerpt_text: The Hebrew yom can refer to daylight (1:5a), to a 24-hour period (1:5b), or to an unspecified time period (2:4b, “When,” literally in the day; cp. Exod 20:8-11).
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: The Tyndale commentary notes the lexical range of Hebrew yom, explicitly citing 2:4b as an instance where yom denotes an indefinite period rather than a 24-hour unit — directly addressing the apparent contradiction between the six-day narrative and the single-day summary.

pd_work.resource: John Haley, An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874)
pd_work.author: John Haley
pd_work.note: Haley discusses the 'in the day' idiom in Genesis 2:4 and the question of whether Genesis 1 and 2 present compatible or contradictory creation timelines.
